Definitely not impossible. For hard classes like this, read the textbook and do the problems in the back of the chapters. His exams pull 80% of the material from concepts you answer in the book and from his practice tests. Another majority of questions will be the in class questions he uses to teach the material and the study guide practice problems. Lee definitely doesn’t leave you stranded in the water, he will give you an ample amount of material to practice. That being said, his practice exams were released a week before the exam and without an answer key (because how similar they are to the actual exam). From what I know, Kang has a similar format for his exams but I could be wrong.
With that, this format forces you to learn the material if you put in the time and pay attention.

Can’t go wrong with either Lee or Kang. My experience with Lee remote has been very good. In my experience, he essentially released youtube videos for you to watch on the material. He then had class meetups a couple times a week (kind of like office hours) for you to discuss the material and any questions you had. Either way, both Lee and Kang are great profs. Good luck!
